sections.h2: Options for a quick Kingsport sale
sections.html:
Three paths are open in Kingsport: list with an agent, arrange a sale with someone you know, or sell for cash to a buyer who takes the property in its current state. Cash often wins when the house needs repairs or a deadline is near, whether that is a tax date or a move.

The city belongs to the Tri-Cities and spans Sullivan and Hawkins counties, which means many steps hinge on where your parcel lies. Assessor, register of deeds and tax lookup all change with the county.

  • Listing: right for a house that shows well, if you can wait while the buyer's loan is approved.
  • Private sale: you still need a closing agent and a deed with no problems.
  • Cash purchase: you set the closing date, and the buyer takes on repairs.

Kingsport held an estimated 57,530 people on July 1, 2025, up 3.6 percent from April 2020. Its land area of 52.6 square miles works out to roughly 1,054 people per square mile.

  • Homes lived in by owners: 60.1 percent
  • Typical value of an owner's home: $234,100
  • Monthly owner outlay with a mortgage: $1,387
  • Middle gross rent: $907
  • Middle household income: $52,490
  • Households: 25,021

Nearly every resident is in Kingsport City Schools, which includes Dobyns-Bennett High School. Neighborhood names buyers search include Lynn Garden, Colonial Heights, Rock Springs, Bloomingdale and Cliffside. A house near the Eastman complex, the downtown Academic Village or the Holston Valley Medical Center campus has a selling point, so mention it. Workers commute 19.1 minutes on average.

sections.h2: City property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The city sends its own property tax bill. For 2026 it is due on or before November 30, 2026, which means a house that closes before then should have the bill paid at the table. Later, penalties accrue on a fixed schedule that city officials cannot waive.

Penalty schedule for unpaid city tax
DatePenalty on unpaid city tax
December 1, 20262%
January 1, 2027Another 2%
Each month afterAnother 1% until paid

Payment options: eCheck online with no charge, card with a 2.75 percent fee, mail, or in person at the Customer Service Center, 415 Broad Street. The city takes no payments by phone, but questions go to 423-343-9860.

The city rate was $1.67 per $100 in 2025 and $1.99 in 2024. Sullivan County reassessed in 2025 after its previous round in 2021.

Phone whichever county assessor covers your parcel. Sullivan County's Assessor of Property works from 3411 Highway 126, Blountville (423-323-6455). Hawkins County's is at 110 East Main Street, Rogersville (423-272-8505). Mailing address changes also go to the assessor, and neither a missed notice nor a value dispute excuses paying late.

Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, can seek state tax relief. On 2026 bills the income cap is $38,470 from 2025, and the value counted is limited to $33,600. A disabled veteran rated 100 percent service-connected, or a surviving spouse, has no income test and a $175,000 value limit. Kingsport adds up to $40 off city tax for those who qualify. The state's number is 615-747-8871.

Sullivan County's Register of Deeds sits at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 101, Blountville, and answers at 423-323-6420, weekdays 8 to 4:30. The state levies transfer tax at $0.37 per $100 of price, plus $0.115 per $100 on new mortgage debt beyond the first $2,000.

Who pays the transfer tax is a contract question. When any piece of the property reaches into Hawkins County, ask the title company which register records the deed before you fix a closing date.

Kingsport wants permits for roofs, decks, porches, additions, finished basements or attics, sunrooms, new electrical or plumbing and replacement water heaters or furnaces. You can paint, swap cabinets or lay flooring without one, and fences need none either. An owner who lives in the house may buy permits for work done personally after signing a Homeowner's Affidavit.

Landlords may handle cosmetic work themselves, though electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits need a contractor with a state license. Jobs under $25,000 call for just the city business license; bigger ones need a State of Tennessee contractor's license. Reach the Building Division at 423-229-9393. Permit fees can be paid online, not by phone.

sections.h2: Building on a lot or replacing a house
sections.html:
Kingsport applies the 2018 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Plumbing, Property Maintenance and Energy Conservation codes, the 2017 National Electric Code and its own zoning ordinance. Someone eyeing a vacant lot or a teardown runs into those rules first.

A new house begins with an Erosion and Sediment Control permit from the Traffic Department, which doubles as the driveway permit; call 423-229-9487 to book a site visit. Next comes zoning, with plat approval from Planning for lots in a Planned Development. Then the residential plans go to 415 Broad Street for review, and the sewer tap fee is due when the building permit is issued. State law lets a homeowner build one new house every two years.

sections.h2: What changes when you sell for cash
sections.html: When a lender is involved, closing waits for loan approval and an appraisal, and the buyer might ask you to fix what the appraiser flags. Cash takes both out, so title work and the tax bill set the date. Before choosing a buyer, find out which county holds your parcel, the balance on the city bill and your lender's payoff figure. Those three answers frame every offer.

A late Kingsport bill grows on a predictable schedule: 2 percent on December 1, another 2 percent on January 1, then 1 percent monthly. City staff cannot waive it, and a lost notice is no defense. Near the due date with a sale underway? Have the title company pay the bill out of your proceeds at closing so the penalties never begin.

The city bill is separate from anything the county may send, so treat them as two checks. Ask the city for its balance and the right assessor about the rest, and jot down both before signing a contract.

Collect the deed, the latest tax notice, a lender payoff letter and permit records for roof, deck, addition or water heater jobs. A past project with no permit should be disclosed to your agent or buyer early. Did you do work yourself? Hold on to the Homeowner's Affidavit you signed for the Building Division, which shows the permit was pulled correctly.

faqs.q: When does Kingsport city property tax come due?
faqs.a: The current bill is due on or before November 30, 2026. After that, 2 percent is added December 1, another 2 percent January 1, and then 1 percent each month.

faqs.q: Is property tax relief available to seniors in Kingsport?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, may qualify under the state program if income is within limits, and Kingsport adds a rebate of up to $40. The 2025 income cap is $38,470.

faqs.q: Which county is my Kingsport house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city lies in Sullivan County, with a western section in Hawkins County. The city's tax lookup has you choose a county, and that county's assessor answers value and address questions.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Kingsport sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $0.37 per $100 of price. Your contract says who pays.

faqs.q: Does replacing a water heater in Kingsport need a permit?
faqs.a: Yes, installing or replacing a water heater needs a plumbing permit. Fences and cosmetic updates do not.
